tasks.gr11-computer-architecture-t2: Topic: Computer Architecture. Cover the Von Neumann architecture model (CPU, memory, input/output connected by buses), the components of the CPU (ALU, CU, registers including the program counter, instruction register, and accumulator), the three types of buses (data bus — carries data; address bus — specifies memory location; control bus — carries control signals), the fetch-decode-execute cycle, and the memory hierarchy (registers → cache → RAM → secondary storage). Ask Grade 11 learners to label architecture diagrams, explain bus functions, describe the fetch-decode-execute cycle step by step, and compare different levels of the memory hierarchy.
tasks.gr11-software-engineering-t2: Topic: Software Engineering and SDLC. Cover the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) phases: requirements analysis, system design, implementation (coding), testing, deployment, and maintenance; modular design (dividing a solution into independent modules with single responsibilities); the difference between unit testing, integration testing and system testing; the purpose of technical and user documentation; and version control concepts. Ask Grade 11 learners to identify the correct SDLC phase for a given activity, explain why modular design improves maintainability, distinguish testing types, and state the purpose of specific documentation artefacts.
tasks.gr11-databases-sql-t2: Topic: Databases and SQL. Cover the relational database model (tables, fields/columns, records/rows), primary keys (unique identifier for each record), foreign keys (linking tables), basic SQL statements: SELECT (with FROM, WHERE, ORDER BY, LIKE, AND/OR), INSERT INTO … VALUES, UPDATE … SET … WHERE, DELETE FROM … WHERE, and aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX). Ask Grade 11 learners to write or complete SQL queries, predict query output from a given table, identify primary and foreign keys in a schema, and fix SQL syntax errors.
tasks.gr11-sql-integration-t2: Topic: SQL Integration with Programming. Cover connecting a program to a database (connection string, opening/closing connections), executing SQL queries from code (parameterised queries to prevent SQL injection), binding query results to forms/controls, validating data before inserting into a database, and basic database normalisation (1NF — no repeating groups; 2NF — no partial dependencies; 3NF — no transitive dependencies). Ask Grade 11 learners to complete code that reads from a database, explain why parameterised queries are safer, identify a normalisation violation in a table, and trace a form-to-database data flow.
